A '''code cylinder''', '''data cylinder''', '''rank cylinder''',<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> '''rank code cylinder''',<ref name="GG1-2">[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope'', Second Edition]]</ref> '''command cylinder'''<ref name="EGWT" /> or '''data probe'''<ref name="GFT">''[[Galladinium's Fantastic Technology]]''</ref> was a common security device used by military [[Officer/Legends|officers]], corporate executives, and [[Politics/Legends|politicians]]. It acted as a sophisticated [[Keycard/Legends|keycard]] for secure areas. Each cylinder contained its user's personal security clearance codes and data. It was not uncommon for high-ranking personnel to own multiple code cylinders, each with their own encrypted access codes. They were used extensively in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], particularly to facilitate security measures. The devices, usually carried within a pocket or on one's belt, used the same interface as a [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] [[Scomp link/Legends|scomp link]].

Additionally, code cylinders could be reprogrammed. In situations where it was impossible for a [[Slicer/Legends|slicer]] to be physically present and hack a security door, they sometimes elected to reprogram the cylinder instead. Cylinders were programmed with countermeasures such that a failed reprogramming caused the data to become irretrievably corrupted.

==Description==
Code cylinders were small, cylindrical devices that were a combination of [[Scomp link/Legends|scomp link]] and [[data terminal]]. The code cylinder allowed an individual to interface with [[Computer/Legends|computers]], [[Droid/Legends|droids]], and [[security lock]]s. Military [[Officer/Legends|officers]] had their identity and security clearances encoded onto the device using custom-programmed coding and [[identification chip]]s. Voice, retinal, and [[Dermatoglyphic pattern|dermatoglyphic]] records were also stored on the code cylinder, and could be read and verified by specialized scanners.<ref name="EGWT" />

The code cylinders were inserted into a security terminal or [[Dataport/Legends|dataport]], following by the owner inputting a personal access code. A cylinder being used to access computers or facilities that it was unauthorized for automatically triggered an alarm. An alarm would also be sounded if the pass code was incorrectly entered. Upon a correct input, the clearances would be confirmed by the computer network attempting to be accessed before clearance was granted. The automated system allowed for secure and limited access to a facility, while also decreasing the number of [[Security guard/Legends|security guards]] needed on duty at any time.<ref name="EGWT" />

==History==
During the [[Jedi Civil War]], the [[Sith officer]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Doel Scherp]] was entrusted with a code cylinder that contained the command codes for the [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] systems of [[Darth Revan's flagship]]. In approximately [[3957 BBY]], a team of Republic [[Agent/Legends|agents]] stole the code cylinder from [[Scherp's Estate]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sernpidal/Legends|Sernpidal]], and took the device to a rendezvous point with the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Fleet]], on the Republic's border with the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]]. The Fleet subsequently used the information contained within the cylinder to [[Capture of Darth Revan|attack]] the [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], and capture [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]].<ref name="TBODR" />

In the city of [[Depatar/Legends|Depatar]], code cylinders were used to carry the [[permit]]s citizens were required to have.<ref name="cp">{{LivingForce|Clouds of Genarius: Clouded Paths}}</ref>

In the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], the number of code cylinders issued to personnel reflected their rank and importance within the Empire. Higher-ranking officers with access to multiple commands and facilities were issued with several code cylinders while lower-ranking officers generally only had one. Regulations stipulated officers displayed their code cylinders in their front [[Imperial officer's uniform/Legends|uniform]] pocket next to their [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank plaque]]. [[Technician/Legends|Technicians]] and [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] carried their single code cylinders in pockets, on their [[Belt/Legends|belts]], or affixed to a chain hung around their neck.<ref name="EGWT" />

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Empire instituted a policy of issuing updated code cylinders at least once a [[Standard month/Legends|month]]. This was an effort to prevent stolen cylinders that had fallen into [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] hands from being used to infiltrate Imperial facilities. Electronic records were kept of a code cylinder's activity, including access to facilities and any computer file that was accessed by it. The records were routinely monitored by [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] and [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] [[Agent/Legends|agents]] to attempt to expose Rebel agents that had infiltrated the Empire.<ref name="EGWT" /> 

Code cylinders were used by the [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] allied to the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]. Some [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] member states used similar technologies to achieve the same result, including coded [[Identichip/Legends|identification cards]] and [[electronic key]]s.<ref name="EGWT" />

==Behind the scenes==
In the films, the code cylinders worn by [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] were small pen-like radiation [[Wikipedia:Dosimeter|dosimeters]].<ref name="Set Piece">{{InsiderCite|96|Set Piece|Set Piece: Death Star Conference Room}}</ref>
